# CB RULES for the editor-compositor (GENERATED 2026-11-22 by tools/slice_rules.py from CB_RULES.md; do not edit)
CB_RULES.md is the master and wins. This file holds the rules that touch your job. Read it instead of the whole book. If a rule you need seems missing, grep CB_RULES.md for the word; do not read it top to bottom.

## RULE NO. 1: MAKE A RICK-QUALITY VIDEO. If this fails, everything is wrong.
(CB 2026-11-11: "no1 rule is to make ricks quality video", "if is fails everything is wrong")
- [ ] Every rule below serves this one. Following a workflow step, passing a gate or ticking a box never excuses a result that is below Rick's.
- [ ] THE TEST, on every picture and every clip before CB sees it: put ours next to a Rick frame of the same kind of shot (same shot size, same kind of place). Ask plainly: would this pass as a frame from his channel? Look at story clarity, world detail, light and shadow, reflection, colour, acting, camera.
- [ ] If ours is clearly weaker, it is NOT done. Fix it, or tell CB exactly what is still below Rick and why. Never present it as finished.
- [ ] If a workflow, tool or note leads to a result below Rick, the workflow is wrong: stop, say so, and use the method that reached the quality before (the airfield way).
- [ ] RICK'S QUALITY IS THE TARGET; TOKENS ARE A GUIDE (CB 2026-11-16: "ricks quality is the target"). The tier budget (11a2) guides how we spend; it never decides that a film may be below Rick. Never skip a check, drop a step or deliver weaker work to stay inside a budget. When reaching Rick's quality needs more than the budget, the lead says so plainly at 80 % with what it needs and why, and asks CB; the hard cap is still passed only on CB's yes.

## HARD RULE NO. 2: NOTHING GENERIC PASSES. EVERYTHING IS ULTRA DETAILED. (CB 2026-11-11: "Can we add rules hard rule. Nothing generic wont pass. Everything need to be ultra detailed")
This is a gate, not advice. A frame that fails it is not shown to CB and not rendered further.
- **Generic = fail.** A plain box, ball tree, flat one-colour surface, typed font, filler word, star in place of a word, empty prop, standing or floor-sit pose where the story needs a real action, or a set that could belong to any film.
- **Every object in frame is specific to THIS story** and built from real parts, down to the small things: a wallet has pockets, stitching, a photo and flies that fly out; a board carries a real blueprint; a cart carries the ride's name; a loop under construction shows the crane and the missing piece.
- **Scale is checked:** trees about a quarter of the hero structure, a vehicle small around its rider, characters as large in frame as Rick's.
- **Poses are specific:** seated means a chair-sit with knees forward, sleeping means slumped with a tilt; body moves come from the trained motion library.
- **The test before CB sees it:** put the frame beside Rick's and name five specific details in every main object. The five details of every prop and of the hero object are written FIRST, in `PROPS.md`, and CB OKs that list before the set build (11a step 1b, check 2). If you cannot, or if Rick's shows a kind of thing ours lacks, it fails. Fix it first.
Full detail list: section 3, "PREMIUM DETAIL IN EVERYTHING".

## 11. THE LEAN PIPELINE AND THE TOKEN RULES (CB 2026-11-15 after the armor film: "how we can optimized that is not burn too much tokes and quicker to make", "or what takes so much time and not worth", then "yes please do."). Wins over every older pipeline line in this file and in SKILL.md.
Why: the armor film (63.5 s) cost 1.66 billion tokens, 41 helpers and 22.7 working hours. Measured: about 750 million went into a still-picture storyboard with judge rounds that CB rejected when he saw it move; 97 % of all tokens were re-reading (every step a helper takes re-reads everything it has seen so far); builder 1 alone cost 184 million because one conversation ran 13 hours. Target for the next film of the same quality: at most 450 million tokens and 12 working hours. Since 2026-11-16 the budget comes from the film's QUALITY TIER (11a2), per finished minute.

### 11a. The lean pipeline (the order of work)
0. THE LEAN WAY IS THE DEFAULT FROM THE NEXT FILM (CB 2026-11-17, after the two lean test rounds: "its improve alot and also safe tokes.", then "Yes, apply the rule changes" on the card "Make the lean way the default for new films now?" and "yes" in the thread). Proof and numbers: `episodes/_tests/lean_2026-11-17/` (REPORT.md, r2/REPORT_r2.md, RULE_CHANGES_PROPOSAL.md). Where a step below names separate board, build-out, camera-director and fix-round helpers for one stretch, this paragraph wins:
   - ONE BUILDER PER STRETCH does the board, the build-out AND the camera, in one session. The camera plan (stations, holds; no "travel" overrides unless a whip) is LOCKED and passes `python tools/film_plan.py check` (with its window speed check, `--window a-b`) BEFORE the first render. Fix rounds stay inside the same builder while its time box lasts (11b T9b); after the time box a fresh builder continues from STATE.md (11b T2). Measured: lean r1 + r2 = 1 builder, 0 helpers, 0 cuts, camera p90 18.2 px/f against 21.8 for the old pipeline.
   - KIT REUSE FIRST: sets, cast, props, moves, bike and vehicle fits, grade and captions from the earlier films before anything new is built. Hard Rule No. 2 stays: every reused object gets FIVE story-specific details (lettering, wear, place marks, period parts, props) before it counts as done (ESTIMATE: not measured in the test; the reused traffic-lights kit already had them).
   - DEPARTMENT AGENTS ONLY FOR NEW KIT: set-builder, character-artist, props-hero, animator and the camera-director are called when the stretch needs a NEW set, person, prop, move, or a camera idea the builder cannot find in the move library (11h), not by default.
   - ONE COMMAND PER STRETCH CYCLE: `bash tools/run_stretch.sh <film.json> <a-b>` (bake, plan check with the window speed check, GPU render, frame checks with the driver and body rows, 11i detail gate, cam_track numbers, one log).
1. STORY AND VOICE, THEN THE PICTURE PLAN. One story unless CB asks for a choice; facts checked; voice recorded; `words.json`; then `PICTURE_PLAN.md` (11d): what the viewer sees on each word, written for this story.
1b. THE FIVE PRE-BUILD CHECKS (CB 2026-11-16: "ok add this to the worklow", approving the coordinator's list of five steps "that make the quality before the build, not after"). Why: the last films went over budget and needed extra rounds because the faults were found after the gate (traffic lights: the car rebuilt after the gate, every stretch rendered twice for the camera; braking lines: the world at half Rick's detail found on v7; armor: the stills passed what the moving film failed). Each check is cheap and catches one of those before anything is built. Steps 2 and 3 are QUICK OKs in the chat (CB says yes or strikes a line), never a polish round; THE ONE GATE (step 2) stays the only review gate. They come out of the tier budget (11a2); the budget itself does not change.
   1. REFERENCE PACK, BEFORE THE SCRIPT IS LOCKED. The `rick-researcher` picks 5-10 Rick frames PER BEAT from `references/` (same job in the story, same shot size, same kind of place, same light), writes `episodes/<name>/refs/REF_PACK.md` (beat, frame file, what to take: camera, staging, light, detail) and one small sheet per beat. It PICKS from the studies we have; it does not study Rick again (11b T8). The writer locks the script only when every beat has its frames. Every later side-by-side (checks 3-5, Rule No. 1) uses these frames, so no helper hunts for a reference again. Frames stay private.
   2. HERO OBJECT MODEL AND PROP LIST, CB OKs BEFORE THE SET BUILD. After the picture plan, the `props-hero` builds the hero object model (three views, in its character's fist, beside the Rick frame of the same kind of object) and writes `episodes/<name>/PROPS.md`: every prop the plan names, who holds it, its real size, its era, and FIVE SPECIFIC DETAILS for this story (Hard Rule No. 2). The lead posts the hero sheet and the list in the chat; CB says yes or strikes a line. No set or prop is built before that yes.
   3. ONE-PAGE LOOK CARD, CB OKs IT. Before any set is built, the lead makes `episodes/<name>/LOOK_CARD.jpg` (one page, phone readable): the colour world (12c: its name, 3-5 hex, the one accent), the key light direction and the time of day per place, the period and place, each beside 1-2 Rick frames of the same light from the reference pack. It is the summary of LOOK_BIBLE.md (11c), not a new document. CB says yes or changes a line in the chat; the look pack (11c) is built from it.
   4. HOOK TEST FIRST. Before the rest of the film is built, the hook builder builds frame 0 and the first 10-15 s AT FULL DETAIL (look pack, dressing at the 11i gate, light, the acted gag, voice and captions) from the hook stretch's camera plan (2b). The lead puts it beside the hook frames of the reference pack (one sheet and one side-by-side clip at full speed). If ours is not clearly as strong as Rick's (Rule No. 1: frame 0 as the hook picture, story readable with the sound off, world detail, light, camera), STOP there: fix the method on the hook and test again; never start the other stretches on a method that loses. When it passes, the hook clip goes to CB in the chat at once (to see, not a gate; CB's yes at the one gate covers it) and the other stretches start.
   5. CHECKS AFTER EVERY SCENE, NOT ONLY AT THE END. Each scene (each stretch render, board and polish alike) runs in its run.sh, in the same call: `node tools/frame_checks/check.mjs`, `node tools/camsafe/validate.mjs` and a Rick side-by-side sheet (ours beside its beat's reference pack frames, small, 11b T3). A FAIL or a weaker-than-Rick sheet stops that scene and is fixed before the builder reports; the other scenes go on. The final still gets the full run (section 7).
2. THE ONE GATE: THE WHOLE FILM ROUGH, PLUS THE HOOK MOVING. As soon as the hook test passes (1b, check 4), one builder per remaining stretch starts at once (section 10) with a cap of 60-90 minutes and brings 2-3 real three.js key frames for EVERY line of its stretch: no polish, stand-in cast allowed. The hook is the 10-15 s of the hook test (1b, check 4), at full detail, with voice and captions. CB sees the picture plan, the whole board with its line check (every scene already through its checks, 1b check 5) and the moving hook together, and says yes or no. Nothing but the hook is polished and no judge runs before this gate. Why both: the armor film showed that stills cannot prove motion or camera (CB rejected what the stills had passed); the Moonrakers film showed that polishing one scene for a day before CB has seen the whole film wastes the day (CB 2026-11-14: "til now i dint see the storybaord", then "Board all 20 lines now"). This replaces the hook-frame gate of section 0.
2b. THE CAMERA PLAN, BEFORE ANY STRETCH RENDERS IN MOTION (CB 2026-11-16 after elevator, Monopoly, braking lines and fake surgery all came out with a fast, jumpy camera: "previousd work didnt have this issue now the issue is back. you need to know before this happen. so avoid it"; "you can not make one mesurement as norm since every episode is different"). Why it came back: the old stage 5 (camera-director + `film_plan.py check`) had no place in this lean list, so the stretch builders put one camera station on every picture-plan row (about 80 in 74 s), and "one flying take" (11f) turned the cuts between them into whips. The films before the lean pipeline (lightning spear, goldrush) had the camera step and did not have the fault. Rule:
   - A PICTURE-PLAN ROW IS NOT A CAMERA STATION. Rows say what the viewer must see on a word; one camera move flows through several rows (follow the thing that moves, push in, rise up the tall thing, cross the set).
   - The `camera-director` writes each stretch's camera from the built sets BEFORE its builder renders motion: one flowing idea per place, with the reason for every move from this scene, written in the stretch's CAMERA_NOTE.md.
   - The scene decides the numbers, not one norm: `python tools/film_plan.py check` runs in every stretch's run.sh before any render and prints the camera bands as a WARNING list. A camera band may be outside only with this scene's reason in CAMERA_NOTE.md. A station teleport (a jump in one frame inside a take) and an unplanned whip are always FAIL.
   - CAMERA V2 ON EVERY NEW FILM (CB 2026-11-16 "Yes, fix and re-test"; proof reel episodes/_tests/camera_rules_2026-11-16/CAMERA_TEST_V2.md, CINEMATOGRAPHY.md section 7). Every new film.json starts with `"camera": {"v2": true}`: travel time grows with distance (1.5 s + 0.25 s/m, up to 6 s), speed is checked against the subject, stations too close are flowed through (WARN), close rests keep drifting, `whip: true` is a capped 9-frame whip, eases are timed on picture speed. Measured on the 12-move test: parked 25 % -> about 1 %, near-to-far peak 33 -> 19, the builders' 1-station-per-second hop -> one flowing move. Films already rendering without the switch stay as they are (without it the bake is byte-identical to before). Every camera v2 WARN is read and fixed or given its scene reason in CAMERA_NOTE.md.
   - THE COMPARISON BEFORE THE REST RENDERS: the lead measures the first moving stretch with tools/measure/cam_track.py and watches it at full speed beside a Rick clip of the same kind of scene (references/reports/CAMERA_TEST_ALL_2026-11-16.md: our approved lightning spear parks as much as the faulty films, so it is not the model) before the other stretches render. If ours moves faster, hops more or feels less controlled, stop and fix the plan; never render four more stretches on it.
3. BUILD OUT AND POLISH THE STRETCHES from the approved board, in parallel (section 10), from ONE shared sets folder from the first day (never a copy of the sets per stretch), with the strong colours already in (11c). CB's approved board is the FLOOR: a polished frame keeps every story element its board panel shows (props, characters, the gag, the named thing) and the light of its chapter; the builder checks board beside polish before reporting, and every scene runs its checks as it renders (1b, check 5).
4. CB'S NOTES IN BATCHES. The lead collects all notes on a version, runs the automatic checks first, then sends ONE fix round per version. Aim: two rounds.
5. SOUND, then THE GRADE as the last picture step, then delivery.
ONE FOLDER PER FILM (CB 2026-11-15: "never create so many subfolder. for one keep same name and create inside subfolder with version"). A film lives in ONE folder, `episodes/<name>/`, named after the film, never after a prompt or a task. Stretches, versions, fixes and tests go INSIDE it: `episodes/<name>/s2/`, `episodes/<name>/v3/`, `episodes/<name>/_tmp/`. Never a sibling folder such as `<name>-s2`, `<name>-s4a-raid`, `_ridefix_tmp_s4a` or `continue-<name>-from-handoff...`. Every helper brief names its subfolder inside the film folder. Temp folders are deleted when their stretch lands. At delivery the film folder keeps the final video, the scripts, the notes and the code; frame folders, old versions and logs are deleted. DELETE DIRECTLY, WITHOUT ASKING, as soon as the final is approved (CB 2026-11-15: "next time please delete directly after everything final keep only neccessary files and final files"): keep the final video(s), scripts, notes, code, cast, refs, sets and sound; delete every frame folder, old version, old animatic, log and temp folder. Then decode the kept final once to prove it plays.
TAKEN OUT FOR NOW (CB 2026-11-16, after seeing the cost table of the armor film: "ok lets take it out for now. update the skill"). These are not done at all, not even as a test, until CB asks for one of them by name in a new message:
- LIGHT ROUNDS ON THE STORYBOARD (day light, glints, shadows, lantern glow worked on still pictures by the lighting-director): 159 million tokens and about 4 hours on the armor film, rebuilt for the moving film anyway. Light now comes from the LOOK_BIBLE colour targets and light colours per place written BEFORE the sets are built (11c), and the stretch builders set it in their own takes. The lighting-director is called only to write those targets.
- EFFECTS ROUNDS ON THE STORYBOARD (dust puffs, light beams through holes, glow passes worked on still pictures by the vfx-artist): 104 million tokens and about 3 hours, same reason. Effects now come only from the "effect or gag" column of the picture plan (11d) and are built by the stretch builder inside its take, from `templates/pieces/` where a piece fits. The vfx-artist is called only for one effect the picture plan names that no piece covers, inside a stretch, on the moving clip.
- (BROUGHT BACK 2026-11-20, see section 3 "BLENDER IS BACK") THE BLENDER LAYER (shiny metal, glass, materials, the RunPod Blender render): 76 million tokens and about 6 hours plus RunPod for a gain that is hard to see on a phone. No Blender pass of any kind, also not for a shiny hero object, until CB asks. The look-finisher and 3d-designer are not called. `episodes/armor-no-holes/blender_metal/RUNPOD.md` and `rules/parked/BLENDER_PARKED.md` (every Blender rule taken out of this file on 2026-11-16) are the record of how to do it when CB asks.
A STEP TAKEN OUT KEEPS ITS GUARD (CB 2026-11-16, same note). Before a step is taken out of the pipeline, or a rule changes how the camera, the cast or the cut works, the lead writes in one line what that step protected and which remaining step now protects it (a check in run.sh, a brief line, a helper). No guard named, no change. Check this list when a fault CB once fixed comes back: the camera fault of 2026-11-16 came back because "department rounds on still pictures" were taken out and the camera plan went with them.
Also not in the pipeline any more:
- Department rounds on still pictures BEFORE the gate (camera, light, props and effects each sending fix rounds on a storyboard) and judge loops. On the armor film three such rounds chased judge scores of 5.5 and 6.8 and none of that work reached the film; on Moonrakers six judge and fix rounds went into 7.5 s while 18 lines were not started. A judge runs at most ONCE per version, AFTER the gate, on the moving clip and its sheets; never judge, fix, judge more than twice without CB seeing the version. The lead still LOOKS at the check sheets before CB sees anything (section 7 stays).
- A repaint of finished sets. Colour is decided before the sets are built (11c).

### 11b. Token rules (every helper and the lead)
- T1 READ ONLY YOUR SLICE. A helper reads `rules/dept/<its department>.md` (made by `python tools/slice_rules.py`) and the files its brief names. It never reads the whole of CB_RULES.md or SKILL.md; when it needs one more rule it greps for the word. Only the lead reads the whole book, once per session. LEAN DEFAULT (2026-11-17): the stretch builder too reads only its slice (its rows of the picture plan, the guards of 11a2, the 11h camera moves, 11i), never all of CB_RULES, SKILL and HANDOFF at its first step (measured: lean r1 carried about 100 k tokens of that first read through every later step).
- T2 A FRESH HELPER FOR EVERY FIX ROUND. A helper does one build or one fix round, then it ends. Before it reports it writes `STATE.md` in its work folder (at most 60 lines): what is built, the files and frame folders, the numbers measured, what is weak, what is open. The next round is a NEW helper that reads STATE.md and the notes. Never resume a helper that already did a round: each resumed step re-reads its whole history. LEAN DEFAULT (2026-11-17): the one stretch builder of 11a step 0 does its own fix rounds while its time box lasts (T9b); this rule applies when the time box ends. (This replaces "one builder who stays through every fix round" in section 10.)
- T3 NUMBERS BEFORE PICTURES. Anything a script can measure is checked by a script that prints numbers: a figure cut by the frame edge, the named thing in frame on its word, floor share, saturation and brightness, frozen frames, loudness. A helper opens a picture only when a number fails or for the one final look. Pictures are looked at small: one sheet at most 1,600 px wide, at most 4 pictures per check round, never full-size frames one by one.
- T4 ONE COMMAND PER CYCLE. Render, sheets and measurements run from ONE script call. A long run goes in the background and the helper ends its turn; it does not wake up to wait, poll or look at a log. Every wake-up re-reads everything.
- T5 SHORT REPORTS, DETAIL IN FILES. A helper's report is at most 25 lines: done, numbers, weak points, files. Tables and lists go into a file the report names.
- T6 THE SMALL MODEL FOR MECHANICAL WORK. Rendering, joining, measuring, merging, fact checks, sound mix runs and file moves go to a helper on the smaller model (Agent tool `model: sonnet` or `haiku`). The main model is for story, acting, camera and look decisions. LEAN DEFAULT (2026-11-17): no helper by default. A stretch builder starts at most ONE small-model helper, and only for render and measure (no judging, no building), with its own time box (ESTIMATE: render and measure are about 10-15 % of a stretch's tokens).
- T7 A FRESH LEAD SESSION PER PHASE. Story, build and finish are three sessions, each started from HANDOFF.md. The lead never reads a helper's transcript and never pastes long tool output into the chat when a file path will do.
- T8 NOTHING BUILT TWICE. Before a helper builds a tool, a set part or a move, it greps `tools/`, `templates/` and the last episode for one that exists. Studies of Rick are done once and live in the rules and `references/`; a film does not study him again unless CB names a new question. Also before a new check or rig: grep `tools/` and `templates/` for one made the same day (lean r2 wrote scale_check.mjs while body_check.mjs was being written in another thread).
- T9 MEASURE EVERY FILM. At delivery the lead runs `python tools/token_report.py` and writes the totals into HANDOFF.md: tokens per helper, working hours, and the three most expensive helpers with the reason. A helper over 60 million tokens is a fault to explain.
- T9b TIME BOX PER BUILDER AND PER HELPER (lean default, 2026-11-17): about 60 steps per 7 s stretch window; when it ends the builder writes STATE.md and stops. Measured: lean r1 65 steps 16.9 M tokens, r2 72 steps about 15 M (with four extra CB notes and a new check tool). EXPECTED TOKENS with a reused kit: about 2-4 M per film second (measured: r1 2.4 M/s; r1 + r2 together about 4.6 M/s), so about 150-250 M for a 60 s film when the kit exists (ESTIMATE), against 720 M measured for traffic lights; a film that needs new sets and cast costs more (ESTIMATE: +100-200 M). The quality tiers (11a2) stay the budget cap; these are the expected spend inside them.

## 12. THE CREATIVE EDGE: MATCH RICK ON CAMERA AND WORLD, BEAT HIM ON CHARACTER ACTING (CB 2026-11-16: "ok add it", approving the suggestion "we match Rick on camera and world and beat him on character acting"; with "i want something creative agent to add that thinks more out of the box")
Why: Rule No. 1 makes Rick the floor, and a floor alone makes a copy. The old study law of the skill already asked for a CREATIVITY GAP (every idea we take from him carries one invention of our own; every film has something his films have no equivalent of), but no step of the pipeline produced it. We keep his pacing, script pattern, camera moves and world density (sections 1, 6, 11e-11h) and win where his films are thin: his characters mostly stand, point and react with one face.
- [ ] 12a CHARACTERS THAT PERFORM. Every beat gets ONE small acted gag on its word: a double take, a fumble and catch, a proud pose that backfires, a too-careful tiptoe, a slow glance to the lens, a held breath that ends in a cough. It is built from the acting faces (char2d FACES: think, concentrate, aim, lipBite, holdBreath, browUp, nervousSmile, glanceCam, proud), the grips and the funny movement library (`pick({ action, feeling, energy, persona })`), written as an ACTING SEQUENCE with times (section 5, CHARACTER ACTING) and played by the animator as an episode move. It reads with the sound off. It keeps the older limits: one action or one feeling per beat (section 9), never over key narration, the face calm first and changing on the word, dead still once settled, the cast's own personality (CAST_PERSONALITY.md). No two beats of one film use the same gag mechanism.
- [ ] 12b ONE SIGNATURE SHOT PER FILM. One picture Rick would never make, built around THIS story's hero object: ride inside it, the set transforms in one move (the cell folds out of the board, the bell turns into the stage), the object at a scale or from an angle only this story allows. It sits on the TURN or the CLIMAX row, is entered and left by a camera move (never a hard cut), and still passes the camera-safe, frame and grounding checks; kid-safe. It may also be the film's impossible view (11f), but it must be ours: never a shot from a Rick film. It is proven first, alone, like a hero object (Ultra: its own helper, 11a2; Standard and Premium: the first thing its stretch builder proves).
- [ ] 12c A COLOUR WORLD PER FILM. Each film has its own bold palette, written in LOOK_BIBLE.md before any set is built (11c): a plain name ("tin-toy red and pool-table green"), 3-5 key colours as hex, the ONE loud accent on the hero object, ONE SIGNATURE COLOUR ON THE HERO ONLY (CB 2026-11-17: "what you can learn fromhere to make our video better", then "yes can add all"; source: the "Miner Who Fed Ghosts" prompt, project files rules/miner_prompt_2026-11-17.md: the old miner's red neckerchief is the only red on any person): the hero character wears one signature colour that no other person in the film wears, checked on the cast sheet (in a one-red film this is usually the red), and how the palette SHIFTS with the mood of the story (start, turn, low point, payoff), riding on the light kinds the plan already has. It keeps the 11c numbers (saturation, night brightness at least 0.31, one red, faces white by day), Rick's natural grass and sky unless the story's world is not natural (a toy, a board game, a dream), and it is never the palette of the last film. It goes on the LOOK CARD that CB OKs before the sets (11a step 1b, check 3).
- [ ] 12d WHO MAKES IT. The `creative-director` agent (agents/creative-director.md, slice rules/dept/creative-director.md) runs ONCE per film, right after the script and voice and before the picture plan is final. It writes `episodes/<name>/CREATIVE.md`: one acted gag per beat with its mechanism, three signature-shot ideas with one picked and why, the colour world, and up to five more fresh ideas (a running gag, a set that tells a joke, a transition through the hero object, a sound idea, a title idea). It reads only the script, words.json, CAST_PERSONALITY.md and its slice; it never builds and never re-studies Rick (11b T8). The writer and the lead take what fits into PICTURE_PLAN.md (columns "acted gag" and "signature"); CB sees CREATIVE.md with the picture plan at the one gate and can strike any idea. Cost: about 1-3 M tokens.
- [ ] 12e THE GUARD. The creative edge never overrides a CB rule: Rule No. 1 (each picture beside a Rick frame of the same kind of shot; weaker = not done), Hard Rule No. 2, the locked cast and views, the camera rules, the facts of the story. Never copy Rick's story, characters, gags or shots; his frames stay private. Every tier (11a2) carries it: Standard = the gags and the colour world, the signature shot reusing kit parts; Premium and Ultra build the signature shot new.

## 7. Before sending to CB (sign every line by looking, not by the gate report)
- [ ] STORYBOARD TO CB AS EARLY AS POSSIBLE (CB 2026-11-13 04:56-04:57 Bangkok, fireworks test thread, after waiting about 5 hours with nothing to see: "why you dont give me a preview first?", "at;east a stroyboard", "so i can judge", "important rule add to the skill storybaord to judge as quickes a spossible."). Every film shows CB a storyboard (all panels, graded, beside the Rick frames) as soon as the first full pass exists (plan check 0 FAIL, nothing broken; narration words under each panel), and an animatic with sound as soon as that is ready, before further judge loops, the still approval and any long render, so CB can judge early (since 2026-11-15 this is THE ONE GATE of 11a step 2). It is clearly labelled "storyboard for your judgement" with one line on what is still missing. Then the crew keeps working while CB looks: the judge scores, the stills and the animation follow, and CB's notes go in first. This REPLACES the old "never show a rough block-in" rule and the "only 8.5/10 or more goes to CB" bar for storyboards and previews; the 8.5 bar and the 12 scores are used by the judge only as the quality tier says (11a2): at most once per version, after the gate, on the moving clip. Never let more than about an hour pass on a film without CB having something to look at.
- [ ] UNIVERSAL CINEMATIC ANIMATION DIRECTOR, 15 PERMANENT STANDARDS (CB 2026-11-13 02:23 Bangkok: "about 80% of that master prompt is universal... Keep this as Claude's permanent master instruction"; full text in project files rules/CB_cinematic_master_2026-11-13.md). The crew works as a professional stylized 3D/2.5D studio and decides direction, camera, sets, acting, materials, light, physics, VFX and transitions from the story itself. The 15: personality, natural animation, facial acting, dialogue and lip sync, original gags, narrative world building, modelling and mechanics (primitives only for blocking), materials, cinematic lighting (motivated key, soft fill so shadows are never black, controlled rim, contact shadows, atmosphere, a grade for the story and time of day; no flat even brightness, over-saturated grass or flat skies), VFX, cinematography, physical consistency, continuity, stylized art direction (cast simple and clean, world rich), quality validation. Each has its full rule in sections 2-6; this line ties them together. Never force objects, effects or gags into a scene that does not need them. Never say an effect is built when the code only has a placeholder. (Its Blender tool line is parked with Blender.)

On the gate board and on every version the lead checks each shot against its reference frame: 1 the camera matches the intended subject and shot type; 2 the main action reads at once; 3 models and machinery have enough detail; 4 materials look right; 5 lighting and depth match the scene; 6 characters framed and posed right; 7 no floating, clipping or broken geometry; 8 VFX have coherent shape, direction and depth; 9 the shot fits the shots around it. Right objects but the wrong visual story = fail (the loaded projectiles, not the wheels).

- [ ] THE FOUR FAULTS OF THE PLANE-EATER FILM (CB 2026-11-22, on plane_eater_blender_v1: « il y a plein d'autres erreurs comme des objets mal placés qui rentrent en collision, le personnage principal était trop gros et il manque de fluidité dans ses mouvements, pas seulement les personnages, les assets manquent clairement de fluidité, ils ont l'air saccadé si on regarde bien, globalement l'environnement est bon mais le jeu de lumière et d'ombre fait encore défaut, n'oublie pas que le rendu Rick ressemble à un jeu vidéo, il est très fluide »). Checked on EVERY film before CB sees a moving version, in the draft AND again in the Blender frames:
  1. NOTHING COLLIDES, EVERYTHING IS PLACED: no object, prop or character passes through another (hand props through bodies, characters through tables, seats, wings; props sunk in or floating over their support). A contact check on the moving film, not on stills only; a collision found = fix before the next step.
  2. THE CHARACTER IS IN SCALE WITH HIS WORLD: the main character's height against the door, chair, table, vehicle and the other characters is measured (CAST_KEYS heights in metres against the set's real sizes) and compared with Rick frames of the same shot kind; a head that fills the frame in shot after shot is too big. Close shots are chosen by the camera, not by an oversized card.
  3. FLUID LIKE A VIDEO GAME (Rick's render looks like a game engine: very smooth): every moving thing moves on every frame with eased, continuous motion: characters, held props, set pieces, effects, camera. No stepped or snapping props, no pose pops, no card that jumps between two drawings without an in-between, no camera hitch at a join. Guard: a per-object motion check over the whole film (position change per frame: no zero-then-jump pattern, no frame-to-frame jump above the move's own speed) + the lead watches the film at full speed AND frame by frame; "looks jerky if you look closely" = FAIL.
  4. LIGHT AND SHADOW PLAY: the environment being good is not enough; each shot needs readable light design: a clear key direction, cast shadows of characters and props that fall on the ground and on each other, contact shadows, light/shade contrast on the subject (lit side, shade side), dapple or shaped light where the story has it, and the light changing with the story clock. Flat even light on cards and props = FAIL. Compared beside Rick frames of the same light.
- [ ] THE CODED FRAME HAS REAL METAL, REAL SURFACE RELIEF AND A REAL SKY (CB 2026-11-15 on lightning spear final v1: "quality can be much better. more details. iron speeer need metallic detail and the sky looks weired", "gold angle more detailed. stomr bell made metallic gold. even the floor looks to vector with no textuire. the trees also, the bell wheel also", "what cause that you dindt make it right in the beginning?"). WHY IT HAPPENED: every set used the kit's flat 3-step toon material (no metal can shine in it), surface textures were flat colour pictures with no relief, the sky was a gradient with flat cloud blobs, trees were simple clumps, and the lead judged detail on 135-360 px sheets without a side-by-side with Rick; the armor film's metal had come from a Blender layer, which the lean pipeline switched off. RULE: (1) metal, gold, bronze, glass and wet things use the kit's PBR path (physical material with an environment map from the scene's own sky, brushed or hammered normal map, clearcoat on gilt), never the toon material; (2) stone, brick, tile, wood, cobbles, mud and bark carry a normal or bump map plus colour variation, never a flat painted picture; (3) the sky has volume (layered lit clouds with soft edges and depth), per light kind; (4) trees have trunks with bark, branch forks and many leaf clusters with light and shade; (5) every hero object the voice names (here: spear, bracket, wire, bell, bell wheel, gold angel) is a detailed model with at least 10 named parts, made FIRST, alone, and checked full size beside a Rick hero object before any stretch uses it; (6) the LEAD looks at 8 random frames per stretch at full width (at least 540 px wide each) beside Rick frames before CB sees a version: small sheets are only for staging.

### from 4. Characters
- [ ] LIMBS ACT LIKE HUMAN LIMBS: bend only at real joints and only the way a person's can (elbows back, knees forward), can do everything a person does, hands and feet end ON what they touch. ("All limbs are acting like human limbs can move and do everything")

### from 5. Movement and acting
- [ ] NO FLICKERING FLOOR, NO SLIDING WALK, NO BODY INSIDE FURNITURE (CB 2026-11-15 on the goldrush final v2: "0.11 floor is flicker, the seller also sliding insted of walking. also his body is in the table", "0.32 at the river 0.54 floor flickering", "0.59 the miner is in the table", "the women have shade on her face and also is in the table. please avpoid these"). (1) FLOOR AND GROUND NEVER FLICKER: shadows, light patches and textures on floors, decks and ground stay stable from frame to frame while the camera moves (no shadow-map shimmer, no lamp flicker that jumps the whole floor); a lamp may flicker only as a small, slow change on what it lights. Measured on the rendered frames before CB sees them (flicker scan of the floor region: frame-to-frame change no bigger than the camera's own move explains). (2) A WALK IS A WALK: a character who changes place walks with planted feet whose stride matches the distance travelled (motion library walk, foot locked per step); never a card gliding while the legs cycle or stand. (3) NO BODY INSIDE FURNITURE: counters, tables, chairs and tubs are solid: a character stands or sits BESIDE or BEHIND them with the whole body on the right side of the surface, seen from the camera; a seated character's legs go under a table only where the table is open. Checked per rest by the frame checker (body and head inside a set mesh) and by eye on a zoom sheet. (4) FACES CLEAN: no shadow, shade band or dark patch on a face from a table, hat, prop or light (extends NO HAT OR HAIR BRIM SHADOW ON FACES).

### from 11i. THE WORLD AT RICK'S DETAIL: a measured detail gate and a dressing step, standard for 
- THE GATE (every place, every light kind, BEFORE any stretch builder starts and again on the final): render 3 fixed test cameras per place and kind (a wide, a medium at character height, a low close) and run `python tools/measure/density_check.py --style 3d <frames>`; PASS = edge density median >= 0.14 and no test frame under 0.08 (RE-MEASURED 2026-11-17, CB "do both": the first floor of 0.18 came from ONE Rick clip, Drivers Filming 0.184; over 8 Rick clips with tools/measure/detail_density.py at 1 frame per 2.5 s the film medians are 0.099-0.184, median of medians 0.14, lower quartiles 0.07-0.13; density_check.py's own 3d gate, fitted on 193 of his frames, is 0.14. Our approved armor film measures 0.117 and lightning spear 0.168, while elevator v2 measures 0.234 and was judged 4.9/10: edge density is a FLOOR against empty frames, never a quality score, and haze or depth of field that Rick also uses lowers it, so it is not chased with clutter or sharpening), shapes (G2) >= 700, empty cells (G3) at or under Rick's median. The numbers go in `sets/STATE.md`; a place that fails is not handed to the builders.
